title: POC weekly: INT8/FP8 tradeoff checkpoint - Aurora HealthTech
summary: Weekly POC sync to review INT8 vs FP8 pilot results across quality KPIs and latency/throughput deltas. Discussed calibration steps, mispredictions/regression triage, and next actions for a ~2-week cutover test with clinical de-identification workload. Agreed to run a controlled A/B with 1k validation samples and share RCA spreadsheet.
topics: Quality delta numbers (ROUGE/acc proxy) between FP8, INT8, baseline FP16
Latency p50/p95 changes and cold-start behavior
Fallback policies and A/B plan for production trial
Security/PHI handling, KMS, audit logs requirement
next_steps: Redwood to share the detailed comparison spreadsheet (per-case diffs) by 2026-05-10
Aurora to supply the 1k labeled validation payload set by 2026-05-11 (sanitized)
SE to run a dedicated batch of per-layer calibration profiles and post results by 2026-05-13
Schedule a 30-min follow up after validation run on 2026-05-15
action_items: Priya Desai: export per-layer activation histograms, add suggested quantization knobs (due 2026-05-13)
Jordan Mills: share comparison spreadsheet + test harness link (due 2026-05-10)
Aisha Khan: provide sanitized 1k validation set and confirm PHI scrub process (due 2026-05-11)
Dr. Lena Cho: review top-20 regression cases and provide priority list (due 2026-05-12)
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-07
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Participants: Jordan, Priya (Redwood); Lena, Marcus, Aisha, Tom (Aurora)

Auto-summary (auto): Quick sync on quantization pilot - initial quality deltas look small but some edge-case regressions in clinical note normalization. Latency improvements observed with INT8 at p50 but p95 regressions with cold KV cache misses.

[00:00] Jordan Mills: All right, hi everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on this POC. Priya will run through the perf and quality numbers, then we'll go through the regression examples that Lena flagged.
[00:12] Priya Desai: Hey all, yep I'll share my screen in a sec. Just to set expectations we ran three axes: baseline FP16, FP8 (per-channel), and INT8 with calibration. The dataset was your sanitized anonymized notes set of ~8k records we ran across the week.
[00:28] Dr. Lena Cho: Quick note, a couple of those records weren't fully de-id'd -- we circled them in the drive. Aisha is following up on the scrub pipeline.
[00:36] Aisha Khan: yeah sorry we found two with MRNs, we removed them and reuploaded. should be clean now.
[00:42] Priya Desai: cool, thanks. So quality first: aggregate ROUGE-like proxy (we used your F1-match proxy) saw a mean drop of 0.6% for FP8 and 1.5% for INT8 versus FP16 on the full set. Median was smaller, pl 0.2% for FP8. But the important thing is the tail -- the top-20 regressions are concentrated on rare templated notes where numeric rounding changes the structure.
[01:10] Marcus Reed: when you say "rounding" are we losing decimal precision on dosages? that's a red flag for clinical.
[01:15] Priya Desai: good catch. In a few templates the tokenization and quantization produced slightly different continuations around numbers. We think it's not the model hallucinating but numeric representation shifts caused by per-layer scaling.
[01:28] Tom Bauer: That could be a compliance issue, we need to check any change that alters clinical dosage phrasing.
[01:34] Jordan Mills: Understandable. One of the mitigation options we discussed was targeted calibration per-layer for the numeric-heavy heads and falling back to FP16 for those specific tokens — effectively a hybrid.
[01:45] [01:45] Priya Desai: Right, we actually prototyped a hybrid path in the runtime. For those sequences flagged by a regex (numbers, mg, ml, mg/kg), we force a FP16 micro-execution. That added ~4% latency for those sequences but eliminated the regression on our sample.
[02:02] Dr. Lena Cho: okay that seems reasonable as long as it's deterministic and auditable. We need audit logs showing when fallback was used.
[02:12] Priya Desai: Redwood console can surface that — there is an event emitted when fallback triggers, and we can add a per-request flag. We'll add the audit log format to the security packet.
[02:24] Jordan Mills: moving to perf numbers: INT8 reduced p50 from 210ms to 150ms on average (~28% improvement) but p95 stayed around 520ms due to cold KV cache misses and some kernel scheduling stalls. FP8 gave ~18% p50 improvement with slightly better p95 at 480ms.
[02:47] Marcus Reed: can you explain the KV cache miss pattern? we saw spikes exactly every ~5 minutes in our telemetry.
[02:53] Priya Desai: yeah those spikes line up with GPU eviction and small batch cold starts — the serving runtime keeps a per-shard KV cache, and if a variant is evicted or if a model variant appears cold (like the hybrid FP16 path), we see extra latency on the first token while KV gets repopulated. For Aurora's tail-heavy bursts, we've seen that show up.
[03:12] Aisha Khan: can we pin the model variant for dedicated pools? we have reserved capacity plans but not sure if that avoids eviction.
[03:19] Jordan Mills: On Dedicated it's much less likely; we can reserve capacity and bump the warmup windows. Also there are autoscale/pre-warm hooks we can add when you anticipate bursts.
[03:30] Tom Bauer: any cost delta numbers? we'd like to compare cost per 1k tokens across variants.
[03:35] Priya Desai: rough numbers: FP16 baseline cost X. FP8 was ~0.72X, INT8 ~0.58X after batching and KV amortization. These are pilot numbers and will change with throughput. We'll export a per-token cost spreadsheet.
[03:52] Dr. Lena Cho: how confident are you in the INT8 numbers? I'm worried about variability across prompts.
[03:58] Priya Desai: It's promising but we saw regression clusters. Our advice is to run a short A/B on the sanitized 1k validation set to measure real-world variance before broader rollout.
[04:10] [04:10] Jordan Mills: let's dig into the regression examples now. Priya, can you show the top three?
[04:14] Priya Desai: sure. Example one: baseline FP16 returns "administer 2.5 mg" whereas INT8 returned "administer 3 mg" in one pass — small but clinically significant. On inspection the token probability mass shifted slightly at the decimal token boundary.
[04:28] Dr. Lena Cho: that's exactly the kind of case that would block us. We need to guarantee no change in numeric precision.
[04:33] Priya Desai: We agree. Fix options: stricter per-layer calibration, hybrid FP16 for numeric tokens, or post-generation deterministic numeric rewriting (not ideal). We prefer calibration + hybrid as the primary path.
[04:46] Marcus Reed: How much engineering effort for hybrid?
[04:49] Priya Desai: we already have a prototype in runtime; production hardening + audit + tests ~2 sprints (4 weeks) for a full hardened rollout, but we can ship a controlled pilot in 1–2 weeks with the A/B harness.
[05:01] Jordan Mills: Security side — Aurora asked about KMS/HSM and audit trails. Aisha, any additional requirements?
[05:07] Aisha Khan: We'll need HSM-backed keys for PHI at rest and in-transit encryption. Also SOC2 evidence, and SSO (SAML) integration. We want request-level tracing retained for 30 days.
[05:18] Priya Desai: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and can integrate with HSMs. Audit events for fallback and model-variant selection are emitted. We'll add the retention policy options to the security packet.
[05:30] Jordan Mills: great. Aisha, we'll share the security packet and you can confirm.
[05:34] Aisha Khan: thanks.
[05:36] [05:36] Tom Bauer: quick question on evaluation metrics — you used a "ROUGE-like proxy" per Priya, is that aligned with our clinical labeling? we care about exact phrasing for certain templates.
[05:48] Priya Desai: For speed we used an F1 token-match proxy; for the A/B we'll run stricter edit distance + custom template checks that Lena's team provided. That will better surface those dosage/regression cases.
[06:02] Dr. Lena Cho: we'll also provide 20 canonical templates that must be exact. If model fails those we'll need to abort.
[06:10] Priya Desai: Understood. We'll bake those into the gate.
[06:14] [06:14] Jordan Mills: timeline check: if Aurora can hand over the 1k validation set by Monday (2026-05-11), Priya will run the A/B and share results by Wednesday (2026-05-13). Then 30-min sync Friday (2026-05-15) to decide whether to proceed with a limited canary.
[06:29] Marcus Reed: sounds good. On canary, we want a max of 5% of traffic and the ability to instant rollback.
[06:35] Priya Desai: rollback is builtin, we also support automatic fallback to FP16 if quality monitors cross thresholds.
[06:42] Dr. Lena Cho: What about model explainability — can we get token-level logits for the failing cases? That will help clinical QA.
[06:50] Priya Desai: We can provide per-token logits for the flagged set; note that's large but feasible for 1k records. We'll include those in the export.
[06:59] [06:59] Jordan Mills: Any blockers from Aurora side right now?
[07:03] Aisha Khan: just KMS confirmation and sanitized dataset. We'll confirm KMS by end of day.
[07:08] Tom Bauer: budget question — if we go with hybrid/FP16 fallback we'll incur a small cost premium; is that accounted for in your pricing model?
[07:15] Jordan Mills: yes the usage meter will reflect hybrid execution; we can show a cost estimate once we have usage patterns from the A/B. We'll also propose a dedicated capacity quote if you want fixed cost predictability.
[07:27] Dr. Lena Cho: I want to flag that product will require a full compliance packet before any production rollout.
[07:33] Jordan Mills: we'll deliver security/compliance packet with SOC2 docs, audit log examples, and the KMS integration guide.
[07:39] [07:39] Priya Desai: last technical note: INT8 stability across different sequence lengths — we saw slightly larger deltas at >1k tokens; Aurora workloads are mostly short but there are some long summaries. We'll include per-length breakdown in the spreadsheet.
[07:55] Marcus Reed: If longer sequences are a concern we may prefer FP8 which gave a better p95 in your numbers.
[07:59] Priya Desai: yes FP8 looked palatable: smaller quality delta and better tail. INT8 gives better cost but more variance.
[08:10] Dr. Lena Cho: So real decision criteria for us: zero-risk on numeric tokens, acceptable tail latency, and clear auditability. If those hold we can run a production canary.
[08:19] Jordan Mills: perfect. We'll treat numeric token protection as a hard gating rule.
[08:24] [08:24] Closing / Recap:
Jordan: action items recap: Priya to share per-layer histograms and the spreadsheet; Jordan to send the test harness link and security packet; Aurora to provide 1k sanitized validation set and prioritize top-20 regressions. Meet 2026-05-15 for decision.
[08:45] Tom: thanks all.
[08:47] Dr. Lena Cho: thanks, good session.
[08:49] Priya: thanks everyone, talk soon.

Notes: transcript includes some auto-caption errors (e.g., KV cache transcribed as "KV cash" in an earlier draft). Attachments referenced during call: "aurora_pilot_spreadsheet.xlsx" (link shared), "redwood_security_packet_v2.pdf" (link pending).
